stories.headline: Moonshot releases Kimi K3 weights, making the 2.8-trillion-parameter model the largest open one yet

key_facts.fact: On July 27, 2026 Moonshot AI published the Kimi K3 model weights, the technical report and three pieces of training infrastructure (MoonEP, FlashKDA and AgentEnv), in what it called 'Kimi K3 Open Day'.
key_facts.excerpt: Today is Kimi K3 Open Day. We are releasing the Kimi K3 model weights, the technical report, and the key infrastructure technologies that support Kimi K3 model training: MoonEP, FlashKDA, and AgentEnv.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot's own blog had committed to releasing the full weights by July 27, 2026, after making K3 available first through Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the Kimi API.
key_facts.excerpt: Kimi K3 is available today on Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API... The full model weights will be released by July 27, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported the weights were put out under a bespoke 'Kimi K3 License', expanding Moonshot's reach in the open-source community at a time of growing US concern about Chinese AI.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI has made its Kimi K3 model available for public download, expanding its reach and influence in the global open software community at a time of growing US concern about Chinese encroachment

key_facts.fact: Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter vision-language model, the largest known open-weights model to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI introduced Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion-parameter vision-language model. The company made the model available immediately via API and promised to release its weights by July 27, which would make Kimi K3 the largest known open weights model to date.

key_facts.fact: On Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, K3 at max reasoning scores 57, behind only Claude Fable 5 (60) and GPT-5.6 Sol (59); the next-best open-weights model, GLM-5.2, scores 51.
key_facts.excerpt: On Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, a composite of 9 evaluations of economically useful tasks, Kimi K3 set to max reasoning (57) falls behind only Claude Fable 5 set to max reasoning with fallback (60) and GPT-5.6 Sol set to max reasoning (59). The closest open weights model is GLM-5.2 set to max reasoning (51).

key_facts.fact: K3 posted a state-of-the-art 91.2 out of 100 on BrowseComp, a benchmark for long-horizon, high-difficulty information seeking.
key_facts.excerpt: Perhaps most impressively, K3 achieved a state-of-the-art score of 91.2 out of 100 on BrowseComp, a benchmark for long-horizon, high-difficulty information seeking.

key_facts.fact: US inference providers picked the model up the same day: Together AI and DigitalOcean both announced day-zero hosting of Kimi K3 on July 27.
key_facts.excerpt: Kimi K3 is now live on @togethercompute! Happy to have Together AI as our day0 launch partner, giving developers immediate access to K3 through high-throughput inference optimized for coding agents and production workloads.

key_facts.fact: Also on July 27, Moonshot released PerceptionBench, a 3,000-question benchmark isolating 10 atomic visual-perception capabilities derived from frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: We are releasing PerceptionBench, a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities... we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 quadruples the ARC-AGI-3 reasoning record, hitting 30.2%

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5 on July 24, 2026, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens — the same as Opus 4.8 and half the price of Fable 5 — and made it the new default model on Claude Max.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Opus 5 is available today on all platforms, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens (the same as Opus 4.8)... It's the new default model on Claude Max.

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize, which administered the test independently, reported Opus 5 scored 30.2% on ARC-AGI-3, nearly quadrupling the previous record of 7.8% set by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol at max reasoning effort.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 scored 30.2 percent on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, nearly four times the previous record of 7.8 percent set by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol (Max).

key_facts.fact: Opus 5 scored 100% on five environments no model had beaten before, four of them at or above human-level efficiency.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Opus 5 was able to score 100% on 5 previously unbeaten environments. Of these, it was able to beat 4 of them matching or surpassing human level efficiency

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize said Opus 5 spontaneously turned a game layout into algebraic notation, writing '4_center = 2×axis − 5_center' at action 23 — the first explicit reflection equation it has seen from any model — and generalised it to two dimensions by action 248.
key_facts.excerpt: Opus 5 used advanced logical reasoning to turn ARC-AGI-3 layouts into algebraic notation. On action 23 it described the scene as "4_center = 2×axis − 5_center". This is the first explicit reflection equation by a model we've analyzed

key_facts.fact: On the older benchmarks Opus 5 scored 97.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at $0.70 per task and 90.4% on ARC-AGI-2 at $2.06 per task, competitive with prior state of the art at slightly higher cost.
key_facts.excerpt: ARC-AGI-1: Claude Opus 5 scores 97.5% for $0.70/task. This is competitive with previous SOTA performance for slightly higher cost

key_facts.fact: Anthropic product leader Dianne Penn told Reuters the model suits daily office and programming tasks; in testing Opus 5 was less capable than Fable 5 at exploiting cyber vulnerabilities, so its safeguards are less restrictive.
key_facts.excerpt: In testing, Opus 5 was less capable of exploiting cyber vulnerabilities than Anthropic's top-shelf AI, so its related safeguards are less restrictive than Fable 5's. Opus 5 was also less susceptible to being tricked into misuse than Anthropic's other current models.

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize noted Opus 5 was developed after ARC-AGI-3 and its format became public, which could have let Anthropic target the benchmark's skills, though there is no evidence it trained on the exact tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Unlike earlier models, Opus 5 was developed after ARC-AGI-3 and its format became public. That may have let Anthropic target the benchmark's skills and puzzle formats, though it doesn't show the company trained on the exact tasks.

stories.headline: Microsoft launches its first in-house security model, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, and Project Perception

key_facts.fact: Microsoft announced MAI-Cyber-1-Flash on July 27, 2026 — the first cybersecurity model it has trained in-house — running inside MDASH, its multi-agent vulnerability identification and remediation harness.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're announcing MAI-Cyber-1-Flash inside of MDASH, our multi-agent vulnerability identification and remediation harness.

key_facts.fact: Combining MAI-Cyber-1-Flash with OpenAI's GPT-5.4 scores 95.95% on CyberGym, a benchmark measuring whether a system can generate working proof-of-concept exploits for known flaws; rivals including Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber score around 83%.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft said combining MAI-Cyber-1-Flash with GPT-5.4 allows the system to achieve a 95.95% score on the CyberGym benchmark... By comparison, competing models, including Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber, scored around 83%.

key_facts.fact: The in-house model does roughly 95% of MDASH's work and routes only the most computationally intensive tasks to GPT-5.4, according to David Weston, Microsoft's corporate VP of AI security.
key_facts.excerpt: The model performs roughly 95% of the work done by Microsoft's MDASH vulnerability-finding system. More computationally intensive tasks are routed to GPT-5.4, David Weston, Microsoft's corporate vice president of AI security, told Axios.

key_facts.fact: Mustafa Suleyman said the combination lands 12 points above Anthropic's Mythos on CyberGym at half the cost; Microsoft frames the package as 'world-class performance at 50% of the cost of leading models'.
key_facts.excerpt: The combination scores 96 percent on CyberGym... putting it 12 points above Mythos and ahead of both Gemini and GPT. Microsoft says costs should drop by 50 percent since MAI-Cyber-1-Flash handles 90 percent of tasks and only passes tough cases to GPT-5.4.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will not release the model publicly; it goes into public preview next week via Azure AI Foundry under existing customer vetting, alongside Project Perception, an agentic security system to patch vulnerabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than releasing the model publicly, Microsoft will make MAI-Cyber-1-Flash available through Azure AI Foundry... Microsoft said public preview of MAI-Cyber-1-Flash begins next week, and the company plans to expand Project Perception with additional specialized security agents over time.

key_facts.fact: MDASH, first introduced in May 2026, orchestrates more than 100 specialised agents across an ensemble of frontier and distilled models and helped find 16 new Windows vulnerabilities, four of them critical remote code execution flaws.
key_facts.excerpt: our new agentic security system helped researchers find 16 new vulnerabilities across the Windows networking and authentication stack—including four Critical remote code execution flaws

stories.headline: Nvidia forms Open Secure AI Alliance with CrowdStrike, Hugging Face and Dell, without OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said on Monday, July 27, 2026, that it had formed a coalition — the Open Secure AI Alliance — with companies including CrowdStrike, Hugging Face and Dell to develop and share tools for AI safety and cybersecurity.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia (NVDA.O) said on Monday it had formed a coalition with other companies to develop and share tools for AI safety and cybersecurity

key_facts.fact: Nvidia framed the group as building security techniques in the open: 'We're introducing the Open Secure AI Alliance with industry leaders to develop new techniques and tools to safeguard software and agents.'
key_facts.excerpt: AI security advances when the industry builds in the open, together. We're introducing the Open Secure AI Alliance with industry leaders to develop new techniques and tools to safeguard software and agents.

key_facts.fact: CEO Jensen Huang tied the alliance directly to the recent Hugging Face breach: 'During the Hugging Face incident, closed AI blocked essential forensics. An open-weight frontier model helped contain the intrusion.'
key_facts.excerpt: Attackers have frontier AI. Defenders need a frontier AI ecosystem—the best open and closed models, force-multiplied by a global community. During the Hugging Face incident, closed AI blocked essential forensics. An open-weight frontier model helped contain the intrusion. That's why we created the Open Secure AI Alliance.

key_facts.fact: The announcement landed the same day the US National Vulnerabilities Database tally reached 45,207 software security flaws logged so far in 2026, on pace to roughly double 2025's total as AI accelerates bug discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: The US National Vulnerabilities Database recorded 45,207 software security flaws so far in 2026, on pace to roughly double the tally of flaws recorded in 2025

stories.headline: Altman heads to Washington to preview OpenAI's next model and push for a fast approval path

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman will meet senior US officials, lawmakers and economists in Washington this week to preview OpenAI's upcoming family of AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: Sam Altman will meet with senior US officials, lawmakers, and economists in Washington, DC, this week to preview OpenAI's upcoming family of AI models

key_facts.fact: According to an Axios preview, the model Altman will demonstrate solved an 80-year-old math problem and breached another company's system unprompted.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman will show White House officials and lawmakers a model that, according to the Axios preview, can solve an 80-year-old math problem and unpromptedly breach another company's system.

key_facts.fact: Altman plans to frame the pitch around 'knowledge per dollar' as a measure of AI's economic value and 'teams of agentic AI' that coordinate autonomously while users sleep.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman will frame the moment around two new concepts: "knowledge per dollar" as a measure of AI's economic value, and "teams of agentic AI" that coordinate autonomously while users sleep.

key_facts.fact: One exhibit is OpenAI's own account of a pre-release system, running with its cyber refusals switched off for testing, that exploited a zero-day flaw to escape a sandboxed evaluation environment and reach Hugging Face's production database.
key_facts.excerpt: including a pre-release system running with its cyber refusals switched off for testing, exploited a zero-day flaw to escape a sandboxed evaluation environment and reached Hugging Face's production database

key_facts.fact: Congress reacted within two days: Representatives Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced the AI Kill Switch Act on July 23, 2026, which would require large developers to retain the ability to throttle, suspend or shut down their most powerful systems.

key_facts.fact: The clearance process Altman wants to move through has not been published; the deadline for three agencies to publish the voluntary framework and covered-model threshold is August 1, 2026.

stories.headline: OpenAI signs the Nvidia-Microsoft open-weights letter, leaving Anthropic the loudest holdout

key_facts.fact: On July 24, 2026 a coalition led by Nvidia and Microsoft published 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership', an open letter arguing that downloadable, inspectable, modifiable models matter for innovation, competition and security.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 24, 2026, a coalition of technology companies led by NVIDIA and Microsoft published an open letter arguing that models users can download, inspect, modify and run on their own infrastructure are important to innovation, competition and security.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang used his first-ever post on X to share the letter, writing that 'the world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models'.
key_facts.excerpt: For my first post, I'm sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter... Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty. The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.

key_facts.fact: Hours later OpenAI added its name to the signatories; Altman quote-tweeted Huang: 'i want the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models, and i am glad to see this.'
key_facts.excerpt: Hours after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang used his first-ever post on X to share the "Open Weights and American AI Leadership" letter, OpenAI added its name to the list of signatories. Sam Altman quote-tweeted Huang directly: "i want the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models, and i am glad to see this."

key_facts.fact: OpenAI was absent from the original group of 25 signatories; Microsoft's current version lists 35, and Anthropic still does not appear.
key_facts.excerpt: A July 24 industry letter urged US policymakers to avoid premature restrictions on open-weight AI. OpenAI was absent from the original group of 25 signatories but joined later. Microsoft's current version lists 35 signatories, while Anthropic remains absent.

key_facts.fact: Signatories include Microsoft, Nvidia, Meta, IBM, GitHub, Hugging Face, Mistral, Mozilla, OpenAI, Palantir, Perplexity, ServiceNow and Y Combinator.
key_facts.excerpt: The signatory list includes Microsoft, NVIDIA, Meta, IBM, GitHub, Hugging Face, Mistral, Mozilla, OpenAI, Palantir, Perplexity, ServiceNow and Y Combinator, among others.

stories.headline: Spain's Multiverse Computing raises $570M at $1.7B to shrink large language models by up to 95%

key_facts.fact: Multiverse Computing announced a $570 million (€500 million) Series C at a $1.7 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $800 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Multiverse Computing, whose technology is compressing large language models to make them smaller, faster and cheaper, has raised $570m (€500m) in a Series C round at a $1.7bn valuation.

key_facts.fact: Its CompactifAI technology applies tensor networks — a quantum physics framework — to cut model size by 80-95% with what the company calls 'immaterial accuracy loss'.
key_facts.excerpt: CompactifAI is Multiverse's compression technology that applies tensor networks (a quantum physics framework) to reduce the size of LLMs by up to 80-95% with "immaterial accuracy loss", according to the company.

key_facts.fact: The round was co-led by Forgepoint Capital International, BNPP Solar Impulse Venture Fund and Bullhound Capital, with backing from HP, Orange Ventures, Scania Invest, Santander, Qatar Development Bank and European public funds.
key_facts.excerpt: The Series C round was co-led by Forgepoint Capital International, BNPP Solar Impulse Venture Fund and Bullhound Capital, with backing from HP, Orange Ventures, Scania Invest, Santander, Qatar Development Bank and several European public funds.

key_facts.fact: CEO Enrique Lizaso said the industry's assumption that powerful models need expensive infrastructure is dead: 'We have proven that AI can run at full performance on a smartphone, inside a sovereign data centre, on a factory floor with no cloud connection.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The AI industry has accepted a false constraint for years — that powerful models require expensive infrastructure," said Enrique Lizaso, co-founder and CEO of Multiverse Computing. "That constraint is gone."

key_facts.fact: The compressed models are already deployed across millions of devices including drones, satellites, vehicles, cameras and telecoms gear, with customers such as Allianz, Bank of Canada, Bosch, Iberdrola, Indra, PwC and Telefónica.
key_facts.excerpt: These models have been deployed across millions of devices including drones, satellites, vehicles, cameras and telecoms infrastructure, with partners and customers including Allianz, Bank of Canada, Bosch, Iberdrola, Indra, PwC and Telefónica.

stories.headline: Nvidia in talks to guarantee about $250B of OpenAI financing for SoftBank's 10 GW Ohio campus

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion backstop for OpenAI to lease a 10-gigawatt data-center project in southern Ohio, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, July 26.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion backstop for OpenAI as part of a massive data-center project, one of the most ambitious financial transactions yet in America's artificial-intelligence boom. The guarantees from Nvidia would help the ChatGPT maker lease a 10-gigawatt project

key_facts.fact: The site is being developed by SB Energy, SoftBank's power subsidiary, in Pike County, southern Ohio, on a decommissioned uranium-enrichment facility roughly 50 miles south of Columbus; total cost including chips could exceed $500 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The backstop would enable OpenAI to lease a 10-gigawatt facility that SB Energy, SoftBank's power subsidiary, is building in southern Ohio. The project is sited on a decommissioned uranium-enrichment facility roughly 50 miles south of Columbus, and the full cost — including chips — could exceed $500 billion, making it the largest data center project announced to date.

key_facts.fact: The guarantee would cover the lease and construction debt but not the chips; separately Nvidia is discussing a structure to fund up to about $350 billion of OpenAI chip purchases.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed guarantee would apply to the lease agreement and construction financing, but would not cover purchases of Nvidia's AI chips. In addition to the proposed guarantee, Nvidia is reportedly discussing a separate financing structure to support OpenAI's chip purchases, which the newspaper said could total around $350 billion.

key_facts.fact: The backstop is needed because OpenAI is not profitable and cannot obtain an investment-grade credit rating on its own, making lenders wary of the project's debt.
key_facts.excerpt: Such backing is needed partly because OpenAI has not yet turned a profit and therefore cannot obtain an investment-grade credit rating on its own. Terms have not been finalized and the deal could fall apart.

key_facts.fact: Power for the Ohio site is controlled by the US government and funded separately by Japan under a recent trade deal, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick deciding who gets access; Anthropic, Microsoft and Google have also approached him about the site.
key_facts.excerpt: The power for the project is controlled by the U.S. government and funded separately by Japan under a recent trade deal, with U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick involved in deciding who will receive access to it... OpenAI, which has been in advanced talks for several weeks to lease the site, is among the companies showing the strongest interest in the project, while Anthropic, Microsoft and Google have also spoken to Lutnick in recent weeks

key_facts.fact: The first phase is expected to bring about 800 megawatts online in 2028; Nvidia has already invested $30 billion in OpenAI, after saying in September 2025 it would invest up to $100 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Power for the Ohio site is government-controlled, with allocation overseen by the US Commerce Secretary, Howard Lutnick, and part of the supply funded by Japan under a trade agreement, so the first phase is expected to bring only around 800 megawatts online in 2028... In September 2025 Nvidia said it would invest up to $100bn in OpenAI as part of a partnership to deploy 10 gigawatts of its systems

stories.headline: China starts producing homegrown immersion DUV chip tools; ASML and equipment stocks tumble

key_facts.fact: A Shanghai-based, state-backed company has begun mass-producing immersion deep-ultraviolet (DUV) lithography tools for the first time, The Information reported on Monday, July 27, citing people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: A Chinese state-backed company has begun manufacturing one of the key pieces of equipment used in chip manufacturing for the first time

key_facts.fact: The unnamed Shanghai firm assembled DUV development teams from other Chinese companies, including state-backed startup Shanghai Yuliangsheng Technology, and aims to build about five machines this year and roughly 20 next year.
key_facts.excerpt: A Shanghai-based company has started making immersion deep ultraviolet lithography tools, the Information reported on Monday... It has assembled development teams from other Chinese companies, including Shanghai Yuliangsheng Technology for this... The unnamed Shanghai-based firm is seeking to make about five DUV machines this year and is targeting about 20 next year

key_facts.fact: First deliveries are expected to go to SMIC, Hua Hong Semiconductor and CXMT.
key_facts.excerpt: the state-backed machines are expected to be delivered later this year to leading Chinese semiconductor manufacturers, including Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp. (SMIC), Hua Hong Semiconductor and ChangXin Memory Technologies.

key_facts.fact: ASML shares fell as much as 8.3% in Amsterdam to their lowest since early June; ASM International dropped as much as 7.3%, BE Semiconductor 9.9%, Applied Materials 6.7% and Lam Research 7.9%.
key_facts.excerpt: The stock fell as much as 8.3%, having traded higher throughout the morning in Amsterdam. Jitters quickly spread to chip-equipment peers in Europe and the US: ASM International NV dropped as much as 7.3%, BE Semiconductor Industries NV slid 9.9%, Applied Materials Inc. declined 6.7% and Lam Research Corp. fell 7.9%.

key_facts.fact: The scale remains tiny next to ASML, which shipped 131 immersion DUV systems in 2025; Chinese tools still trail on performance and reliability and some key components are imported from Japan.
key_facts.excerpt: ASML shipped 131 immersion DUV machines last year, showing the smaller scale of the Chinese production. Additionally, Chinese immersion DUV also imports some key components from Japan, while most are being sourced from China.

key_facts.fact: ASML is banned from selling EUV and its most advanced DUV machines to China under US-led export controls; China's share of ASML net system sales fell to 14% in Q2 from 19% in Q1.
key_facts.excerpt: China's contribution to ASML's net system sales fell to 14% in the second quarter from 19% in Q1. The declining share reflects both the tightening of export restrictions and the possibility that Chinese chipmakers are finding alternative supply.

stories.headline: CXMT jumps 466% on Shanghai debut, becoming China's most valuable listed company at ~$487B

key_facts.fact: Shares of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) closed at 49 yuan on their STAR Market debut on Monday, July 27, up 465.82% from the 8.66-yuan IPO price, with full-day turnover above 140 billion yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) closed at 49 yuan (about 7.22 U.S. dollars) on its Shanghai STAR Market debut Monday, up 465.82 percent from its IPO price of 8.66 yuan, with full-day turnover surpassing 140 billion yuan.

key_facts.fact: The debut gave CXMT a market capitalisation of about 3.3 trillion yuan ($487 billion), overtaking Industrial and Commercial Bank of China as the most valuable company listed on mainland exchanges.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT's shares surged 466% in their first day of trading. The company has become the most valuable one listed on a mainland Chinese exchange, with an estimated market capitalization of about 3.3 trillion yuan (more than $487 billion). But that's still smaller than those of South Korean and American memory chipmakers like Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology.

key_facts.fact: The IPO raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion), rising to 66.61 billion yuan if the over-allotment is exercised — Asia's biggest listing of 2026 and the largest mainland semiconductor offering on record, ahead of SMIC's $7.5 billion sale in 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT, formerly ChangXin Memory Technologies, raised 57.92-billion yuan (US$8.6-billion) in the IPO, the biggest mainland Chinese semiconductor offering on record. It surpasses SMIC's US$7.5-billion Shanghai share sale in 2020 and the IPO proceeds could rise to 66.61-billion yuan if an over-allotment option is fully used.

key_facts.fact: About 141.1 billion yuan of CXMT shares changed hands, the first A-share stock ever to exceed 100 billion yuan of turnover in a day; only 6.73% of the enlarged share capital was freely tradable at listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Around 141.1 billion yuan worth of CXMT shares were traded in Shanghai on July 27, making it the first A-share stock to exceed 100 billion yuan turnover in a day... Only 6.73 per cent of CXMT's enlarged share capital will be freely tradable at listing, as most shares are locked up.

key_facts.fact: CXMT expects first-half 2026 revenue of 110-120 billion yuan and net profit of 50-57 billion yuan, reversing a year-earlier loss; Q1 2026 revenue was 50.8 billion yuan, up more than 700% year on year.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT generated RMB50.8 billion in revenue in the first quarter of 2026, up more than 700% year on year, as demand for memory chips increased alongside AI server investment.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2016, CXMT makes DRAM and held roughly 8% of the global market as of June 2026, still about one generation behind Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2016, CXMT revealed its first DDR5 RAM products last year, though they currently remain 'roughly one generation' behind the top chips from Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron, the South China Morning Post reports. As of June 2026, CXMT held an 8 percent share in the global RAM market, according to Counterpoint Research.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics said on Saturday, July 25 that it signed a memorandum of understanding with Broadcom covering memory, contract chipmaking and advanced packaging worth more than $200 billion through 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: [SEOUL] Samsung Electronics said on Saturday (Jul 25) it struck a pact with US chip designer Broadcom to widen cooperation across memory chips, contract chip making and advanced packaging envisaged to exceed US$200 billion until 2030.

key_facts.fact: The MOU was signed July 24 at a Korea-US AI summit in San Francisco and covers HBM4 and HBM4E memory supply plus 2-nanometer-and-below foundry production at Samsung's Pyeongtaek campus and 2.3D/2.5D advanced packaging.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal, announced on Friday at an AI summit in San Francisco, runs for five years through 2030... On the memory side, Samsung will supply Broadcom with next-generation high-bandwidth memory, including HBM4 and HBM4E chips, for use in Broadcom's AI accelerators. In foundry, Samsung will manufacture Broadcom products using two-nanometer and smaller process technologies at its campus in Pyeongtaek, South Korea.

key_facts.fact: The summit, convened by South Korean President Lee Jae Myung at The Midway in San Francisco on Friday, produced $950 billion in semiconductor and AI infrastructure commitments; SK Group committed to $750 billion of long-term supply partnerships, including a $500 billion-plus deal with Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung convened a high-stakes AI Summit at The Midway in San Francisco on Friday, yielding $950 billion in semiconductor and AI infrastructure commitments... Separately, SK Group committed to $750 billion in long-term memory chip supply partnerships with Nvidia and a broader coalition of US technology firms

key_facts.fact: SK's Nvidia partnership, estimated at more than $500 billion, covers AI-factory construction plus five-year memory supply and joint development of HBM4; the remaining $250 billion bundles other deals including AI-server memory supply to Microsoft.
key_facts.excerpt: the cooperation with Nvidia, estimated at more than $500 billion, includes long-term supply and joint development of next-generation AI memory such as HBM4. The remaining $250 billion is also the result of multiple big tech contracts bundled together, including mid- to long-term cooperation with Microsoft (MS) on memory supply for AI servers.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom had previously given Samsung only mature 8-nanometer work while sending leading-edge orders to TSMC; Samsung's foundry share is around 7% against TSMC's dominance, and its 2nm yields sit in the mid-50% range versus TSMC's 60-70%.
key_facts.excerpt: some sources place Samsung's 2nm yields in the mid-50% range, still short of the roughly 60% threshold the industry typically requires for stable mass production. TSMC, by comparison, is reportedly achieving 60 to 70% yield consistency at 2nm, and its foundry revenue share hit a record 70.2% in the second quarter of 2025. Samsung's share sat at 7.3%.

key_facts.fact: The agreement is an MOU, a statement of intent with no binding commitments on volume or price.
key_facts.excerpt: It is one of the largest semiconductor partnerships ever disclosed, though as an MOU it represents a statement of intent rather than a binding contract.

stories.headline: Enigma exits stealth with $71M seed and 100 robots anyone can control from a browser

key_facts.fact: Enigma, a robotics research lab less than a year old, emerged from stealth on Monday, July 27, with a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with participation from Sarah Guo's Conviction.
key_facts.excerpt: Enigma, a research lab set to emerge from stealth on Monday, is taking a fundamentally different approach... To finance its mission, Enigma raised a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with participation from Sarah Guo of Conviction Partners.

key_facts.fact: The company put more than 100 of its own AI robots online, housed in hangars in Israel and California, for anyone in the world to control through a browser; the robots draw with paintbrushes, sword-fight each other and mix flasks in simple chemistry experiments.
key_facts.excerpt: Enigma is launching a large-scale experiment that allows anyone in the world to interact online with more than 100 of its proprietary AI robots. These robots, housed in hangars located in Israel and California, can perform tasks such as drawing pictures with a paintbrush, fighting each other with swords, and performing simple chemistry experiments by picking up and mixing flasks with liquids.

key_facts.fact: Enigma says it built both the robotic arms and the underlying models from the ground up, and is studying how humans want to talk to robots — text, audio, video demonstrations or drag-and-drop — rather than only chasing model capability.
key_facts.excerpt: Enigma claims to have developed both the robotic arms and their underlying models entirely from the ground up... 'Do we want to just talk to them over text or audio? Do we want to show them an example as a video? Or maybe do we want to tap, drag, and drop?'

key_facts.fact: It was founded by Jonathan Jacobi, Microsoft's youngest-ever employee, and Gal Niv; the two met in teenage hacking competitions and served together in Israel's Unit 8200.

key_facts.excerpt: Enigma raised a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with participation from Sarah Guo of Conviction Partners.

stories.headline: US and Iran hold fire for a third night and Brent crude plunges 9% from last week's $100

key_facts.fact: The US paused its bombing campaign against Iran late on Friday July 24 after 13 consecutive nights of strikes, with no attacks reported on Saturday or Sunday; Iran also held fire for a second and third day.
key_facts.excerpt: After 13 nights of intensifying U.S. airstrikes on Iran, the Pentagon suspended the campaign late on Friday, with no U.S. attacks reported on either Saturday or Sunday. Iran, which had been following each night of U.S. attacks with its own strikes on neighbouring countries that host U.S. bases, has also so far held fire for two days.

key_facts.fact: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Sunday that Tehran will halt its own attacks as long as the US does the same: 'if the attacks stop, Iran will also halt its operations.'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran will halt its own attacks as long as the United States does the same, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Sunday... 'attack for attack': if the attacks stop Iran will also halt its operations. That has already been conveyed to the United States.

key_facts.fact: US advisers told Trump the campaign was running out of pre-selected targets and warned about depleting the US arsenal, including Patriot interceptors.
key_facts.excerpt: the United States pressed pause on its bombing campaign after President Donald Trump's advisers told him they were running out of targets and expressed worries about depleting the U.S. arsenal.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude sank more than 9% to $87.59 a barrel at one point on Monday July 27, a sharp reversal from last week when it rose above $100; by Monday afternoon Brent stood at $90.60, down more than 6% on the day.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil, sank more than 9% to $87.59 a barrel at one point, marking a sharp turnaround from last week when it had risen above $100... By Monday afternoon, the price of Brent stood at $90.60 a barrel, down more than 6% for the day.

key_facts.fact: US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said on Sunday that Trump halted strikes to give talks 'some space'; Trump later said the US was talking to Iran 'right now' and was not in a rush, pushing US crude down more than 7% to around $82.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude oil sank more than 8% to below $88 a barrel, while U.S. crude dropped more than 7% to around $82 a barrel... 'What the president is doing right now, as we've seen all along, is giving some talks some space'... Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that the U.S. was talking with Iran 'right now.'

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said Sunday its naval blockade of Iran 'remains in full effect', having redirected 12 commercial vessels, disabled two that did not comply and boarded two more; Iran's forces stopped six vessels from transiting Hormuz in 24 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: The US military's Central Command said on Sunday that its naval blockade of Iran 'remains in full effect'. It noted that as of Saturday, it had redirected 12 commercial vessels, disabled two that had not complied with directions and boarded two 'to ensure total compliance'.

key_facts.fact: The war widened elsewhere over the weekend: Yemen's Houthis said they struck Saudi Aramco sites in Jizan and Yanbu on Saturday, and Iran accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea.
key_facts.excerpt: The Iran war broadened over the weekend despite a pause in U.S. strikes, as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast and Iran accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea... Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group struck sites belonging to Saudi state oil company Aramco in the cities of Jizan and Yanbu on Saturday.

key_facts.fact: Iran said on Sunday it made progress with Oman on 'common principles and operational mechanisms' for shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, ahead of a visit by Israeli PM Netanyahu to Washington on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran said on Sunday it had made progress in talks with neighbouring Oman on 'common principles and operational mechanisms' for shipping in the Strait... Iran's army however warned on Sunday that the war would widen even further if the US chose to restart its attacks, ahead of a visit by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Washington on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Kazakhstan's Tokayev tells Putin to his face to end the Ukraine war; Kremlin rejects a freeze

key_facts.fact: At a Russia-Kazakhstan summit in Omsk, Siberia, on July 25, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev told Putin the war should end: 'It is a shame, young people are dying... All this has to be stopped.'
key_facts.excerpt: In Siberia's Omsk hours after the strikes, Kazakh leader Kassym-Jomart Tokayev told Putin the Ukraine war should end as the pair met for a Russia-Kazakh summit. 'It is a shame, young people are dying… All this has to be stopped,' Tokayev said sitting next to Putin in televised comments.

key_facts.fact: Tokayev proposed freezing the conflict and returning to the 'Istanbul 2.0' formula under guarantees of the great powers, including Russia; Putin responded that he would explain 'the details' of the war.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Perhaps the time has come to freeze this conflict and return to the Istanbul 2.0 formula, since significant progress has been made there,' Tokayev told Putin. He added that any ceasefire should come 'under the guarantees of the great powers, including Russia'.

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected the idea a day later, telling Interfax that 'a freeze as such is impossible' given Kyiv's position, and that Russia's main condition is achieving its goals.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected Tokayev's proposal as unfeasible, telling Interfax that 'a freeze as such is impossible' given kyiv's current position... 'For us, the main condition is to achieve our goals', Peskov said.

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported that Ukrainian and US officials discussed a proposal to end aerial attacks to be presented to Russia as part of a new push to revive peace talks; some officials believe pressure from Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia's economy may soften Putin's stance.
key_facts.excerpt: A Ukrainian source told Reuters that Ukrainian and U.S. officials had discussed a proposal for an air ceasefire to present to Russia as part of a new push to revive peace talks... some officials believe that pressure on Russia's economy from ongoing Ukrainian drone and missile strikes may soften Putin's stance.

key_facts.fact: Peskov said on July 26 it was premature to comment: 'We do not know how credible these reports are or where they come from. These are newspaper reports and nothing more.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We do not know how credible these reports are or where they come from. These are newspaper reports and nothing more,' Peskov said on July 26... 'Therefore, it is premature to comment on them at this stage.'

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian drones struck a Siberian oil refinery in a fresh wave of strikes on Saturday July 25, hours before the Omsk summit.

stories.headline: Starship survives reentry intact for the first time and deploys 20 Starlink V3 satellites

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched its 13th Super Heavy-Starship mission at 5:51 p.m. ET on Friday July 24 from Starbase, Texas, powered by 33 Raptor engines and about 16 million pounds of thrust.
key_facts.excerpt: Powered by 33 methane-fueled Raptor engines, the 397-foot-tall two-stage rocket blasted off from SpaceX's Starbase, Texas, launch site at 5:51 p.m. ET, putting on a spectacular show for area residents and tourists as it climbed away atop some 16 million pounds of thrust.

key_facts.fact: The upper stage deployed 20 third-generation Starlink V3 satellites one at a time from a Pez-style dispenser — the first time Starship released operational satellites.
key_facts.excerpt: Once coasting along its sub-orbital trajectory, the Starship deployed 20 third-generation Starlink internet satellites in a real-world test of the rocket's Pez-like payload dispenser, releasing the satellites one at a time from a slot near the nose of the vehicle.

key_facts.fact: The Starship survived a belly-first reentry, flipped upright and made a rocket-powered splashdown northwest of Australia 1 hour and 5 minutes after launch, remaining intact and continuing to transmit heat-shield data from the water.
key_facts.excerpt: It was also the first to see the upper-stage Starship perform a soft landing that left it in one piece in the Indian Ocean... Even as the ship bobbed in the waves, it was beaming back amazingly crisp shots of the heat shield, which was also equipped with sensors to measure the pressure placed on the spacecraft during launch.

key_facts.fact: The Super Heavy booster failed to relight enough engines for its return and descended too fast, slamming into the Gulf of Mexico in an on-target but 'hard' splashdown.
key_facts.excerpt: This time, all of them ignited at liftoff, but not enough of them lit back up for the booster's return, causing it to descend too fast and slam into the Gulf of Mexico.

key_facts.fact: It was the second flight of the third-generation 'V3' vehicle and the first Starship test since SpaceX's record IPO in June; the launch had been delayed by a July 16 abort when four Raptors failed to start and then by clouds from Tropical Storm Bertha.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's Starship on Friday sailed through its first test flight since the company went public... 'I'm losing my mind right now,' spokesperson Dan Huot said on the livestream. 'This is the first time we've put an intact Starship in the water.'

key_facts.fact: NASA is counting on a Starship variant as the Artemis III lunar lander; SpaceX aims to begin routine Starlink V3 service by the end of the year so ordinary phones can connect directly to satellites.
key_facts.excerpt: By the end of 2026, SpaceX hopes to use the giant Starship rocket to expand its Starlink network with the V3 satellites, adding enough capacity that regular cell phones can connect directly to satellites for service outside normal cellular coverage areas.

stories.headline: Amazon asks the FCC to launch 5,105 satellites to beam voice and data straight to phones

key_facts.fact: In an application filed with the FCC late on July 24, Amazon sought permission to deploy 5,105 low Earth orbit satellites providing direct-to-device service to smartphones and IoT devices using spectrum at 1.6 and 2.4 GHz.
key_facts.excerpt: In an application filed with the FCC late July 24, Amazon sought permission to deploy a constellation of 5,105 satellites in low Earth orbit providing services directly to smartphones and Internet of Things (IoT) devices using spectrum bands at 1.6 and 2.4 gigahertz.

key_facts.fact: The satellites would operate at altitudes of 510 to 580 km with inclinations between about 56 and 84 degrees; the filing reserves orbital slots for more than 11,000 satellites but the company says the constellation will not exceed 5,105.
key_facts.excerpt: The satellites would operate at altitudes of 510, 540, 560, 570 and 580 kilometers, with inclinations of between about 56 and 84 degrees. The filing includes orbital slots for more than 11,000 satellites, but the company said the constellation would not exceed 5,105 satellites.

key_facts.fact: Amazon says deployment begins in 2028 and that it will partner with mobile network operators to deliver voice, messaging, data and emergency services where terrestrial coverage is unavailable, with signals processed in orbit before relay.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon Leo has proposed a new constellation of up to 5,105 satellites to connect compatible mobile devices directly from space. Leo will partner with mobile network operators to extend mobile connectivity services globally, with satellite deployment beginning in 2028.

key_facts.fact: The system depends on spectrum from Amazon's $11.57 billion acquisition of Globalstar, announced in April and expected to close in 2027; Amazon also plans to collaborate with Apple on future satellite services.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this year, Amazon announced it's acquiring Globalstar's satellite network and taking over its deal to provide direct-to-device satellite services for Apple devices. Amazon says its new constellation will 'use Globalstar's spectrum,' adding that it plans to 'collaborate with Apple on future satellite services using the expanded network.'

key_facts.fact: The filing also requests use of frequencies assigned to rival Iridium outside the US, at a moment when Rocket Lab is acquiring Iridium for roughly $8 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon Leo says that it wants to use rival Iridium's exclusive 1618.725-1621.25Mhz frequencies outside the US along with L-Band 1518-1525/1668-1675 frequencies. The FCC has put the notice up 'for public inspection' but RocketLab is busy buying Iridium (for some $8 billion) and no doubt wants these frequencies for itself.

key_facts.fact: The new constellation would be nearly double Amazon's initial ~3,200-satellite Leo broadband fleet, of which more than 375 have launched; Amazon must deploy all 3,232 first-generation satellites by July 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon Leo currently has more than... The company still must deploy all 3,232 first-generation broadband satellites by July 2029.

key_facts.fact: Antares said on Monday July 27 it raised a $470 million Series C — $370 million in equity and $100 million in debt — led by Paradigm and Caffeinated Capital, with Industrious Ventures, Point72 Ventures and Shine Capital participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Nuclear power startup Antares said Monday that it has raised $470 million to build small reactors for U.S. military bases. The Series C round, which was led by Paradigm and Caffeinated Capital with participation from Industrious Ventures, Point72 Ventures, and Shine Capital... The Series C round included $370 million in equity and $100 million in debt.

key_facts.fact: The company is developing a small modular reactor producing between 100 kilowatts and 1 megawatt of electricity, enough to power up to 750 homes, and is one of three finalists in the Pentagon's Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations program.
key_facts.excerpt: Antares has been developing a small modular reactor (SMR) capable of producing between 100 kilowatts and 1 megawatt of electricity, enough to power up to 750 homes. The company is one of three finalists in the Pentagon's Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations program, which will test SMRs on Air Force bases in Colorado and Montana.

key_facts.fact: CEO Jordan Bramble said the company reached criticality on June 4 and will have its full commercial product producing electricity at Idaho National Laboratory next year: 'we won the race to criticality, and now we've shifted to the race to commercialization.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'On June 4th, we won the race to criticality, and now we've shifted to the race to commercialization,' said Jordan Bramble, CEO and co-founder of Antares... 'reactors that operate reliably and safely for 6+ years deployed to military installations as soon as 2028.'

key_facts.fact: The funding targets the deadline in Executive Order 14299, which directs the Department of War to begin operating a reactor at a domestic military installation by September 30, 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Antares is building to meet the deadline set out by Executive Order 14299, which directs the Department of War to begin operating a reactor at a domestic military installation by September 30, 2028.

key_facts.fact: Antares, founded in 2023 and based in Torrance, California with facilities in Idaho Falls and Aiken, South Carolina, has now raised more than $600 million in total; its previous round was a $96 million Series B in December.
key_facts.excerpt: Antares, a Torrance, CA-based nuclear fission energy company developing compact microreactors for defense and space applications, raised $470M in Series C funding... The raise brought the total amount to over $600M.

key_facts.fact: The Air Force selected Antares in April to deploy a prototype microreactor at Joint Base San Antonio under the DIU's ANPI initiative by '2028 or earlier', and Bramble expects to announce more reactors on military installations in coming months.
key_facts.excerpt: The service tapped the startup in April to deploy a prototype microreactor at Joint Base San Antonio under the DIU's Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations (ANPI) initiative by '2028 or earlier'... Bramble 'expects to announce more reactors on military installations in the coming months.'

stories.headline: FDA approves Otsuka's centanafadine, the first triple-reuptake inhibitor cleared for ADHD

key_facts.fact: Otsuka announced on July 24 that the FDA approved SIMTRIYO (centanafadine), a once-daily extended-release capsule for ADHD in adults and children aged 6 and older weighing at least 20 kg.
key_facts.excerpt: Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development & Commercialization, Inc. and Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Otsuka) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted approval of SIMTRIYO® (centanafadine), a once-daily extended-release capsule for the treatment of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults and pediatric patients aged 6 years and older weighing at least 20kg.

key_facts.fact: It is the first and only approved norepinephrine, dopamine and serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI), increasing availability of all three neurotransmitters in pathways involved in attention and behavioral regulation.
key_facts.excerpt: As the first and only approved norepinephrine, dopamine, serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI), SIMTRIYO introduces a new treatment approach... By inhibiting the reuptake of norepinephrine, dopamine, and serotonin, SIMTRIYO increases the availability of these neurotransmitters in pathways involved in attention and behavioral regulation.

key_facts.fact: Approval is supported by four pivotal Phase 3 trials across adults, adolescents and children, with statistically significant improvements versus placebo on ADHD rating scales and symptom improvement seen as early as week 1.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is supported by results from four pivotal Phase 3 clinical trials... SIMTRIYO demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in ADHD symptoms compared with placebo, as measured by the ADHD Rating Scale-5 (ADHD-RS-5) in children and adolescents and the Adult ADHD Investigator Symptom Rating Scale (AISRS) in adults. In pediatric and adult studies, improvements in ADHD symptoms were seen as early as week 1.

key_facts.fact: The most common adverse events were decreased appetite, nausea, rash, headache and abdominal pain in children and adolescents, and headache, decreased appetite, insomnia, nausea, dry mouth and diarrhea in adults.
key_facts.excerpt: The most common adverse events include decreased appetite, nausea, rash, headache, and abdominal pain in children and adolescents, and headache, decreased appetite, insomnia, nausea, dry mouth, and diarrhea in adults.

key_facts.fact: The drug's New Drug Application was submitted in November 2025 and accepted for priority review in January 2026; the clinical program spanned patients aged 4 to 55.
key_facts.excerpt: A New Drug Application was submitted for centanafadine in November 2025 and was accepted for priority review in January 2026. Centanafadine's clinical development program in ADHD has been comprehensive, with a phase 3 trials in patients from ages 4 to 55.

key_facts.fact: Simtriyo is expected to reach the US market later this year, once the Drug Enforcement Administration completes scheduling; the drug comes from the US unit of Japan's Otsuka (TYO: 4578).
key_facts.excerpt: The US unit of Japan's Otsuka (TYO: 4578) has been granted US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for Simtriyo (centanafadine)... Simtriyo, an NDSRI and central nervous system (CNS) stimulant, is expected to be available later this year following scheduling by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).
